name: Cystoisospora belli

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Oocyst: approximately 20–33 × 10–19 µm, elongated oval, usually with one sporoblast when passed.
Mature forms have two sporocysts; modified acid-fast preparations often show pink-red oocysts.

transmission.detail: Oocysts mature outside the host; ingestion of sporulated oocysts leads to small-intestinal infection and shedding.

life_cycle.detail: Oocysts mature outside the host; ingestion of sporulated oocysts leads to small-intestinal infection and shedding.
Oocysts in stool; shedding may be intermittent.

hosts: Humans are the principal host; no intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide, particularly tropical and subtropical areas.
clinical_significance: Watery diarrhea and malabsorption; prolonged severe infection is important in immunocompromised patients.
specimen: Oocysts in stool; shedding may be intermittent.
diagnostics: Concentration and modified acid-fast staining around 400×; further sampling or molecular methods can assist difficult cases.
differential_diagnosis: Larger and more elongated than Cryptosporidium or Cyclospora; annotate sporulation state separately from species.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Cystoisospora belli — Cystoisospora intestinal coccidian. Watery diarrhea and malabsorption; prolonged severe infection is important in immunocompromised patients.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
